property_summary: Put never reverts when called, regardless of arguments and msg.value.
For any call to Put, the balance of the caller must never decrease; the buggy version without overflow check allows balance to wrap around, decreasing the recorded balance.

After any Put call, the recorded balance of the caller must be at least the Ether sent with that call; the buggy version without overflow check allows balance to wrap around to a value less than msg.value.

For any caller and any msg.value, after Put, the sum of msg.value and the previous balance must be greater than or equal to the previous balance; the bug removes the overflow check, allowing wrap-around that violates this invariant.

After a Put call, Acc[msg.sender].balance plus MinSum must be greater than or equal to Acc[msg.sender].balance (no overflow that wraps below a threshold); the bug allows balance+MinSum to overflow and become less than balance, violating this invariant.
For any call to Put, the stored unlockTime must be >= block.timestamp; the bug version can set unlockTime to a past value less than block.timestamp.
After Put, the stored unlockTime must always be greater than or equal to the block.timestamp at the time of the Put call; the bug allows unlockTime to be strictly less than block.timestamp.

After a Put, if the passed _unlockTime is in the past relative to the block.timestamp at the time of Put, then the stored unlockTime must equal that block.timestamp; the bug version unconditionally uses the past _unlockTime, leaving unlockTime < block.timestamp.

For any call to Put with a past _unlockTime, a subsequent Put with _unlockTime=0 must not decrease unlockTime below a prior reference floor; the bug version resets unlockTime to the immediate past value, violating the floor invariant.

After a Put call, the stored unlockTime equals the maximum of the passed _unlockTime and the block.timestamp at call time, so it is never less than block.timestamp; the bug always stores _unlockTime uncapped, which can be strictly less than block.timestamp.
The unlockTime set by Put must equal the maximum of the provided _unlockTime and block.timestamp; the bug always sets unlockTime to block.timestamp regardless of _unlockTime.

For any call to Put, if _unlockTime is greater than block.timestamp, the resulting unlockTime must be strictly greater than block.timestamp; the mutant always sets unlockTime equal to block.timestamp.

For any call to Put with an _unlockTime strictly greater than the current block.timestamp, the resulting Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime must be strictly greater than block.timestamp after the call; the bug ignores _unlockTime and sets it equal to block.timestamp, violating this when _unlockTime > block.timestamp.

For any Put call where _unlockTime > block.timestamp, the resulting Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime must be > block.timestamp; the bug sets it equal to block.timestamp, violating this when _unlockTime > block.timestamp.

After any admissible Put call, the resulting unlockTime stored in Acc[msg.sender] must be at least the original _unlockTime argument supplied (i.e. it never goes below _unlockTime); the bug sets unlockTime to block.timestamp which can be less than _unlockTime when _unlockTime > block.timestamp.
For any call to Put, the balance of the caller must increase by exactly msg.value; the bug mutant decreases the balance instead.

After any sequence of calls to Put, the sum of all Acc(i).balance over all actors i must be at least the total Ether received by the contract; the buggy subtraction violates this invariant because it reduces balances below the actual contributions.
For any single call to Put, the caller's Acc balance must be non-negative; the buggy subtraction can underflow to a huge value, violating this invariant.

For any address holder, the sum of their Acc.balance plus the contract's own balance is at least the MinSum, but the mutant's subtraction breaks this invariant by reducing the holder's balance while contract balance stays the same.

After calling Put, the balance of the caller recorded in Acc should equal the sum of the initial balance plus the value sent, which the reference satisfies and the mutant violates because it omits the balance increment.

After a successful Put, the contract's total Ether balance should equal the sum of all individual Acc balances, which the reference maintains and the mutant breaks by not incrementing the caller's balance.
For any two consecutive calls to Put by the same sender, the increase in Acc[sender].balance must equal the sum of msg.values sent; the mutant fails because it never increments balance.

After any successful Put call, the contract's ETH balance must increase by the exact msg.value sent, which the reference satisfies but the mutant fails because it omits the balance increment, causing the invariant to break.
After calling Put with msg.value > 0, the balance of Acc[msg.sender] must have strictly increased, which holds for the reference but fails for the mutant because it omits the balance increment.

For any address, after one or more calls to Put, the stored unlockTime must be at least the block.timestamp of the latest Put call; the mutant fails to update unlockTime, so it can remain lower than the latest Put's block.timestamp.

After two sequential Put calls with increasing unlock times from two different addresses, the second caller's unlockTime must be at least the block.timestamp of their Put call; the mutant fails to update unlockTime so the second caller's unlockTime can remain lower than the block.timestamp of their Put call.

After any call to Put, the caller's unlockTime must be strictly greater than the block.timestamp at the time of that Put call if the provided _unlockTime is greater than current block.timestamp; the mutant fails to update unlockTime so it can remain equal or lower.

After any Put call, if the provided _unlockTime is greater than or equal to the current block.timestamp, the caller's unlockTime must be at least block.timestamp; the mutant fails to update unlockTime and can keep a past value lower than the current block.timestamp.

After two Put calls from the same address where the second _unlockTime is greater than the first, the stored unlockTime must be at least the second _unlockTime; the mutant retains the first unlockTime instead of updating it.
Collect can succeed only if the caller's balance is at least MinSum

property_summary: Collect only succeeds when the caller's balance satisfies MinSum
Collect reverts only if the caller's balance is below MinSum.
A withdrawal less than MinSum should not reduce the contract balance, but the bug allows it.
After a Collect, the caller's Acc[msg.sender].balance must not decrease below MinSum unless it was already below MinSum before the call; the bug allows any balance to be reduced below MinSum.
For any call to Collect, if the caller's balance is at least MinSum, the contract balance must not decrease; the bug allows a withdrawal below MinSum, violating this invariant.

After a successful Collect, the caller's balance must never be less than MinSum. The bug removes the MinSum check, allowing the balance to fall below MinSum, which the fuzzer will cause by withdrawing enough.

For any call to Collect, if it succeeds then either the caller's prior balance was >= MinSum or the extracted amount is >= MinSum; the bug removes the MinSum guard so a caller with balance below MinSum can collect small amounts, violating this rule.
Collect only succeeds when the sender's unlockTime has passed.

property_summary: After a Collect call, the total contract ether balance must remain >= minSum unless the unlock time has passed; the bug allows withdrawal before unlock time, causing the balance to drop below minSum when it should not.

After a call to Collect, the caller's balance can only decrease if the current time is strictly greater than the caller's unlockTime; the bug violates this by allowing a decrease even when the time is not greater.

After a Collect call that does not revert, if the timestamp is not strictly greater than the caller's unlockTime, the caller's balance must remain unchanged; the bug allows a balance decrease without checking unlockTime.

After any non-reverting call to Collect, if the caller's balance before the call was at least MinSum and the requested amount, then the caller's unlock time must be strictly in the past (block.timestamp > unlockTime); the bug allows a non-reverting Collect without checking unlockTime.

After a successful (non-reverting) Collect call, the caller's timestamp must be strictly greater than their unlockTime; the bug allows withdrawal without this temporal guard, breaking the invariant that only matured balances can be collected.

property_summary: After a Collect call that executes without reverting, the caller's recorded balance in the Acc mapping must be at least zero (no underflow); the buggy mutant removes the check that _am <= acc.balance, so when _am > acc.balance the subtraction wraps and acc.balance becomes huge, violating the invariant that balance never exceeds the original deposit minus successful withdrawals.

After a successful Collect, the internal balance must not have increased due to underflow; the bug allows withdrawing more than available, causing the subtraction to wrap and acc.balance to become > 2^255.

For any Collect that succeeds, the caller's recorded balance must be non-negative and not exceed the original deposit; the bug removes the _am <= balance check, allowing underflow that makes the balance wrap to a huge number.

For any successful Collect call, the resulting balance of the caller must be strictly less than the balance before the call; the bug removes the check that _am <= balance, allowing withdrawal of more than available which causes a subtraction underflow that makes the resulting balance wrap to near 2^256, violating the decreasing balance invariant.
